title: Encore - What is it like to remember every day of your life, with Michael Yassa, PhD, and Markie Pasternak

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a short winter break, so we're revisiting one of our favorite episodes from the past year.
sentences.zh: 《Speaking of Psychology》节目正在进行短暂的寒假休整，因此我们重温了过去一年中最受欢迎的一期节目。

sentences.en: In May, we talked to Dr. Michael Yassa from the University of
sentences.zh: 在五月份，我们采访了加州大学欧文分校的迈克尔·亚萨（Michael Yassa）博士，

sentences.en: California, Irvine, about his research on highly superior autobiographical memory, the remarkable ability that some people have to remember nearly every day of their life.
sentences.zh: 探讨了他关于“超强自传体记忆”（HSAM）的研究，这是一种极少数人拥有的非凡能力，能够记住他们生命中几乎每一天的细节。

sentences.en: Markey Pasternak, a woman with HSAM as it's known, also joined us to discuss what it's like to live with HSAM and how her memory works.
sentences.zh: 拥有HSAM能力的玛基·帕斯特纳克（Markey Pasternak）也加入了我们的讨论，分享了她带着这种记忆能力生活的感受以及她的记忆运作方式。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoy this episode from our archives.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这期来自我们档案库的节目。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology, we'll be back in January with new weekly episodes.
sentences.zh: 《Speaking of Psychology》将在明年一月回归，继续为您带来每周一期的全新内容。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: Do you remember where you were on April 10th, 1999?
sentences.zh: 你还记得1999年4月10日那天你在哪里吗？

sentences.en: What day of the week was it?
sentences.zh: 那是星期几？

sentences.en: What about the weather?
sentences.zh: 那天天气怎么样？

sentences.en: What were you wearing and what did you do all day?
sentences.zh: 你当时穿着什么，那一整天你都做了些什么？

sentences.en: Chances are you can't answer any of those questions.
sentences.zh: 你很可能无法回答这些问题中的任何一个。

sentences.en: For most of us, our autobiographical memory is a bit of a blur.
sentences.zh: 对于我们大多数人来说，我们的自传体记忆有些模糊不清。

sentences.en: Sure, some special occasions stand out, weddings, birthdays, vacations, along with a bundle of random memories that stick with us for no special reason.
sentences.zh: 当然，一些特殊的场合会让人印象深刻，比如婚礼、生日、假期，还有一些毫无缘由却莫名留在脑海里的零碎记忆。

sentences.en: But for people with highly superior autobiographical memory, or HSAM, every day is memorable.
sentences.zh: 但对于拥有“超强自传体记忆”（简称HSAM）的人来说，每一天都是值得铭记的。

sentences.en: Ask someone with HSAM what they were doing on April 10th, 1999, or the 11th or the 16th, and they'll be able to tell you, along with a bunch of other checkable facts.
sentences.zh: 如果你问一个拥有HSAM的人1999年4月10日、11日或16日他们在做什么，他们不仅能告诉你，还能说出许多其他可以核实的事实。

sentences.en: How do they do that?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: How do the brains of people with HSAM store and retrieve this vast amount of detailed autobiographical information?
sentences.zh: 拥有HSAM的人的大脑是如何存储和提取如此海量且详细的自传体信息的？

sentences.en: What's it like to be able to remember every day of your life?
sentences.zh: 能够记住生命中的每一天是一种什么样的体验？

sentences.en: Is it a blessing or a curse?
sentences.zh: 这究竟是一种天赋还是一种诅咒？

sentences.en: And what can studying this unusual ability teach us about how memory works for the rest of us?
sentences.zh: 研究这种非凡的能力又能让我们了解普通人的记忆是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: You know, you started with a very difficult question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你一上来就问了一个非常棘手的问题，Kim。

sentences.zh: 问题的一部分在于，当我们最初接触到这种现象时，它颠覆了我们对记忆运作方式的所有假设。

sentences.en: So one of the first thoughts was, well, they must be using a different mechanism.
sentences.zh: 所以最初的想法之一是，他们一定使用了某种不同的机制。

sentences.en: But pushed to the extreme, one can imagine that, you know, our regular memory systems just have a degree of variation in them, that it could be part of the regular mechanisms,
sentences.zh: 但推向极端的话，人们可以想象，我们的常规记忆系统本身就存在一定程度的差异，这可能是常规机制的一部分，

sentences.en: just like I said, pushed to the extreme.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，推向极端的情况。

sentences.en: And we're still not sure if they're part of that natural variation or if they're using very distinct mechanisMs. And that's what we're hoping to
sentences.zh: 我们仍然不确定他们是属于这种自然差异的一部分，还是在使用完全不同的机制。而这正是我们希望

sentences.en: uncover in the coming years with some brain imaging techniques and various other methods that look deep into the neurobiology of the brain.

sentences.zh: 但我还能记得，你知道，我七年级时暗恋的那个男孩，我很久没见他了，那天我第一次见到他。

It was a

sentences.en: Tuesday and I could tell you all about that, right?
sentences.zh: 星期二，我可以告诉你关于那天的一切，对吧？

sentences.en: So like they can get, you have more random days that you hold with these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以拥有更多与这些事情相关的随机日期。

sentences.en: But, you know, if I can go real back to, let's say go to that 2007 date, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果我能回到过去，比如说回到2007年的那个日期，对吧？

sentences.en: If I can go back and say, yeah, I saw this guy, you know, at the ice rink because I was a figure skater and he was a hockey player and I like bumped into him there.
sentences.zh: 如果我能回到过去说，是的，我是在溜冰场看到这个家伙的，因为我以前是花样滑冰运动员，他是冰球运动员，我在那里撞见了他。

sentences.en: And I can tell you all about that.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你关于那件事的一切。

sentences.en: I can also piece around the days around it.
sentences.zh: 我还能拼凑出那几天前后的事情。

sentences.en: And that's where the memory kind of starts coming into fruition.
sentences.zh: 记忆就是从那里开始变得清晰起来的。

sentences.en: And so I can say, oh, I went to that ice skating practice that day, even though I didn't usually skate on Tuesday nights over the summer, because I had stayed with another friend
sentences.zh: 所以我可以说，哦，那天我去参加了滑冰训练，尽管我通常夏天周二晚上不去滑冰，因为那天我住在

sentences.zh: 而且再过几天就是她的生日了。

sentences.zh: 所以我当时在陪她，因为前一天刚办完她的生日派对。

sentences.en: So I can like that context kind of comes in and I can start piecing around it.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以把这些背景联系起来，开始拼凑出相关信息。

sentences.en: So sometimes if you ask me like a date, I might be like, oh, wait, I don't know exactly what I did on that day quite yet, but I can go to my nearest go
sentences.zh: 所以有时候如果你问我某个日期，我可能会说，哦，等等，我还不完全确定那天做了什么，但我可以找到最接近的日期，

sentences.en: to date, put the context together and kind of crawl to it.
sentences.zh: 把背景拼凑起来，慢慢回想起来。

sentences.en: And it's like a mental image for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就像是一幅心理图像。

sentences.zh: 我知道患有超忆症（HSAM）的人情况各不相同。

sentences.zh: 我认识一些患有HSAM的朋友，

sentences.zh: 我不是这样的。

sentences.en: I have some synesthesia as well.
sentences.zh: 我还有一些联觉。

sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，它看起来就像是一个巨大的“糖果乐园”棋盘之类的东西。

sentences.en: And there's like people and images and places.
sentences.zh: 还有各种人物、图像和地点。

sentences.en: And it's like this fun place in my brain, I can kind of go to and like hop around in different days.
sentences.zh: 它就像我大脑里的一个游乐场，我可以去那里，在不同的日子之间跳跃。

sentences.en: And I can like zoom in on the days and the years and all in the times and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我可以放大查看具体的日期、年份、时间等等。

sentences.en: That sounds amazing.

sentences.zh: 我应该查证一下。

sentences.en: Dr. Yessa, how many people have been confirmed to have HSAM and how do you find these people?
sentences.zh: 又是一个棘手的问题，Kim。

sentences.en: Another tricky question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 我会给你我们掌握的答案，但有一个前提，对吧？

sentences.en: So I'll give you the answer that we have, but there's a caveat, right?
sentences.zh: 我们目前在实验室中确认的人数不到100人，

sentences.en: So we have identified, it's smaller than 100 that we have identified in the laboratory,
sentences.zh: 但我们也收到了世界各地同事的报告，

sentences.en: but we are also getting reports from our colleagues actually around the world in different countries
sentences.zh: 说有个人找到他们，说自己对过去有极其生动的记忆。

sentences.en: of also having individuals kind of come to them and say, I have this extremely vivid memory of the
sentences.zh: 他们可能没看过《60分钟》的节目，也没读过相关的书或论文，只是觉得这很奇怪。

sentences.en: paSt. And they may not have seen, you know, a 60 minutes piece or read about it in a book or a paper, but just sort of think it's curious.
sentences.zh: 但真正的问题在于，除非像Marky这样经历过测试并得到证实，

sentences.en: But that's really the issue is that until, you know, maybe
sentences.zh: 或者有人看过《60分钟》的报道、读过论文或在课上听说过，否则很难意识到这与其他人有什么不同。

sentences.en: Marky has gone through this exercise and really confirmed it, or somebody has seen a piece on 60
sentences.zh: 所以我猜实际上有很多人拥有这种能力却并不自知，也没有理由怀疑这有什么特别之处。

sentences.en: minutes or read a paper or heard about it in a class, it's really difficult to see this as something different from everybody else.
sentences.zh: 他们可能只是处于极端水平，认为自己记忆力很好，但不会认为这是一种独特的病症。

sentences.en: So my guess is that actually there's a lot of people out there that have it and just don't know, and have no reason to suspect that it's all that different.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会看着周围的人想，为什么其他人的记忆力都那么差，而不是觉得自己才是那个独特的人。

sentences.en: They may just be on the extreme, they might think of themselves as having really good memory, but they may not think of it as a unique condition.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们可能低估了拥有这种能力的人数。

sentences.en: And they might look at others around them and think, well, why does everybody else have really crappy memory, you know, as opposed to them sort of being the unique ones.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它仅限于100人。

sentences.en: So I think we're probably underestimating the number of folks who have it.
sentences.zh: 它更有可能达到数千人，但这仍然是一个足够独特的病症。

sentences.en: I don't think it's limited to 100.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它仅限于100人。

sentences.en: I think it's more likely to be in the 1000s, which still makes it a unique enough condition.
sentences.zh: 它更有可能达到数千人，但这仍然是一个足够独特的病症。

sentences.en: But, but we have to have a better means to, to get those numbers.
sentences.zh: 但是，我们必须找到更好的方法来获取这些数据。

sentences.en: What are the tests like when you're trying to confirm that somebody actually has it?
sentences.zh: 当你们试图确认某人是否真的拥有这种能力时，测试是什么样的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so you've gone through this already, Marky.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以你已经经历过这个过程了，Marky。

sentences.en: And here's the problem with the tests is that the initial phase of the testing was really based on sort of almanac type knowledge.
sentences.zh: 测试的问题在于，最初的测试阶段实际上是基于某种类似年鉴的知识。

sentences.en: Let's pick on something that is can have a veridical record that can be confirmed.
sentences.zh: 我们选一些有真实记录且可以核实的事情。

sentences.en: So public events, things that, you know, it's very clear what the actual answers are.
sentences.zh: 比如公共事件，你知道的，这些事情的实际答案非常明确。

sentences.en: But it turned out as we and we were able to identify a lot of people that way.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，我们确实通过这种方式识别出了很多人。

sentences.en: But it turned out as as time went on, we recognize that there are folks who just this may not be their area of expertise, they may not be very attuned to celebrities
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，我们意识到有些人可能并不擅长这些领域，他们可能对名人不太关注，

sentences.en: in particular, you know, public events, but they have incredibly good autobiographical memory.
sentences.zh: 尤其是公共事件，但他们却拥有极其出色的自传式记忆。

sentences.en: So how do you derive a test that is sensitive to those variations and expertise?
sentences.zh: 那么，如何设计一种能对这些差异和专长敏感的测试呢？

sentences.en: And in fact, that's work that's ongoing in our lab right now, we're trying to devise a more individualized approach
sentences.zh: 事实上，这正是我们实验室目前正在进行的工作，我们试图设计一种更加个性化的方法，

sentences.en: that takes the categories of expertise of the individual, and then selects the questions for
sentences.zh: 它会考虑个人的专长领域，然后为

sentences.en: the tool based on the areas that they have selected in a pre test to say, those are the things
sentences.zh: 该工具选择问题，这些问题基于他们在预测试中选择的领域，即那些

sentences.en: I'm comfortable with.
sentences.zh: 我比较熟悉的领域。

sentences.en: Those are the areas where I think I have a lot of knowledge that are related to my autobiography.
sentences.zh: 那些我认为自己有很多知识储备，并且与我的个人经历相关联的领域。

sentences.en: I was a big TV buff when I was growing up.
sentences.zh: 我小时候是个电视迷。

sentences.en: I love sports, you know, whatever it may be.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢体育，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And then we can be a little bit more sensitive to their special abilities in those kinds of domains.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能对他们在这些领域中的特殊能力更加敏感。

sentences.en: Do people with HCM have above average memories in general, like for facts and figures and non autobiographical knowledge?
sentences.zh: 患有超忆症（HSAM）的人在一般记忆力方面，比如事实、数据和非自传式知识，是否高于平均水平？

sentences.en: That's the part that's really, really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这正是最有趣的部分。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: So it really is just autobiographical.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实只是自传式的。

sentences.en: I know, Mark, he's making that expression that suggests that you wish it was better for everything else.
sentences.zh: 我知道，Mark，他露出了那种表情，好像在说你希望它在其他方面也能更好。

sentences.en: And I think that's the reaction we hear from most people.
sentences.zh: 我想这是我们从大多数人那里得到的反应。

sentences.en: You know, they weren't maybe all that exceptional in terms of their school.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们在学校里的表现可能并没有那么出众。

sentences.en: It's not like they could memorize all Shakespeare and all of these things.
sentences.zh: 并不是说他们能背诵所有的莎士比亚作品之类的东西。

sentences.en: You know, their memorization is really just average.
sentences.zh: 他们的记忆力其实只是普通水平。

sentences.en: And if you test them on standardized memory tests, you know, wordless recall and things like that, it's really just average.
sentences.zh: 如果你用标准化的记忆测试来考他们，比如词汇回忆之类的，结果真的只是平均水平。

sentences.en: It seems to be highly specialized for the person's own narrative, for their own autobiographical memories and events, things that have happened to them,
sentences.zh: 这种能力似乎高度专门化，针对的是个人自己的叙事，即他们自己的自传式记忆和事件，那些发生过在他们身上的事情，

sentences.en: and other things that are related to that narrative.
sentences.zh: 以及与该叙事相关的其他事情。

sentences.en: So if, say, you're studying French in school and you have HSAM, does that mean that you're going to have better memory for vocabulary and verb conjugations, for example?
sentences.zh: 那么，假设你在学校学习法语，并且患有超忆症，这是否意味着你在词汇和动词变位方面会有更好的记忆力？

sentences.en: Not at all, unless you can figure out a way to make French really be part of your autobiographical narrative.
sentences.zh: 完全不会，除非你能想办法让法语真正成为你自传式叙事的一部分。

sentences.en: So if it's, you know, if you've traveled to France and spent time there, it became sort of part of your background in autobiography that I think that that's a possibility.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你去过法国并在那里待过，它成为了你背景和自传的一部分，那么我认为是有可能的。

sentences.en: But just naturally taking it in class, I think the reaction is the same one that you get from everybody else.
sentences.zh: 但如果只是自然地在课堂上学习，我认为反应和普通人是一样的。

sentences.en: I'm not going to remember much until I practice it.
sentences.zh: 如果不练习，我记不住多少东西。

sentences.en: Marky, what was it like to take the test to confirm that you actually have this?
sentences.zh: Marky，参加确认你确实拥有这种能力的测试是什么感觉？

sentences.en: I love this question because not a lot of people ask it.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这个问题，因为没多少人问过。

sentences.en: So that's what's cool about being on this podcast in particular.
sentences.zh: 这就是参加这个播客的特别之处。

sentences.en: You know, I was nervous.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我很紧张。

sentences.en: I was really nervous because for me, the stakes were high.
sentences.zh: 我真的很紧张，因为对我来说，赌注很高。

sentences.en: The stakes for me taking this test were, if I don't, if they ask dates and events that I don't get right,
sentences.zh: 我参加这次测试的赌注是，如果我答不上来，如果他们问的日期和事件我答错了，

sentences.en: I'm going to be excluded from this group of people that I know I belong to.
sentences.zh: 我就要被排除在这个我知道我属于的群体之外了。

sentences.en: And that could give me some sort of solidarity in a community where I feel isolated in a lot of the world because of my memory.
sentences.zh: 这本可以让我获得某种社区认同感，因为我的记忆力，我在世界上很多地方都感到孤立。

sentences.en: So I was really nervous, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很紧张，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And so I was a junior in college at Marquette University.
sentences.zh: 那时我还是马凯特大学的大三学生。

sentences.en: I had just learned the previous semester about HSAM in a class, like you had said in the introduction.
sentences.zh: 就像你在介绍中所说的那样，我在前一个学期刚在一门课上了解到超忆症（HSAM）。

sentences.en: And my professor was confident I had it.
sentences.zh: 我的教授很确信我有这种能力。

sentences.en: Like she was a neuroscientist and a neuroscience professor studying Alzheimer's.
sentences.zh: 她是一位神经科学家，也是一位研究阿尔茨海默病的神经科学教授。

sentences.en: Opposite of what was going on with me.
sentences.zh: 这和我当时的情况正好相反。

sentences.en: And she, you know, she knew a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且她知道很多。

sentences.en: She had done her postdoc at UC Irvine and knew a lot of the folks over there and was like, you, you have.
sentences.zh: 她在加州大学欧文分校做过博士后，认识那边很多人，她说，你，你确实有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: These are the people you need to talk to.
sentences.zh: 这些人就是你需要联系的人。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: And so what I did the test over the phone and I believe my first test was on March 1st of 2015.
sentences.zh: 所以我通过电话完成了测试，我相信我的第一次测试是在2015年3月1日。

sentences.en: And what had happened was my friends actually helped me like kind of practice a little bit.
sentences.zh: 当时的情况是，我的朋友们确实帮我练习了一下。

sentences.en: So what they did was they would throw me like for the week before, like current events randomly.
sentences.zh: 他们在前一周会随机向我抛出一些时事问题。

sentences.en: I'd be like studying for a test and they'd be like, when was the Sandy Hook shooting?
sentences.zh: 我当时正在复习考试，他们会问：桑迪胡克小学枪击案是什么时候发生的？

sentences.en: I'd be like December 14th, 2012.
sentences.zh: 我会回答：2012年12月14日。

sentences.en: And like,
sentences.zh: 就像那样，

sentences.en: you know, just so I get my brain in that kind of like in that mode of like I can do it quick because I can do it if you allow me enough time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，只是为了让我的大脑进入那种状态，让我能快速反应，因为如果给我足够的时间，我是可以做到的。

sentences.en: But, you know, I didn't know how long these researchers were willing to give me to answer the questions.
sentences.zh: 但是，我不知道这些研究人员愿意给我多少时间来回答问题。

sentences.en: And so I had some nice collaborative roommates and friends on campus who were like, we know you have this.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一些很棒的室友和校园里的朋友，他们说，我们知道你有这个能力。

sentences.en: We're going to help you.
sentences.zh: 我们会帮你的。

sentences.en: We got this, you know, and the test ended up going well.
sentences.zh: 我们能搞定，你知道的，测试结果最终很顺利。

sentences.en: But to kind of jump on what Dr.
sentences.zh: 但接着Yassa博士刚才说的话，

sentences.en: Yassa was saying as well, is that it's a really difficult thing to test because I was one of the youngest people they had ever tested at the time back in 2015.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常难测试的东西，因为在2015年当时，我是他们测试过的最年轻的人之一。

sentences.en: So they were asking a lot of questions that were not relevant to me and they were not in my time frame.
sentences.zh: 所以他们问了很多与我不相关的问题，而且不在我的时间范围内。

sentences.en: So they asked me, you know, gosh, I'm just trying to think, you know, when the Oscars were in 97,
sentences.zh: 他们问我，天哪，我正在努力回想，你知道，97年的奥斯卡是什么时候，

sentences.en: I didn't know that because I was three years old and I did not care about the Oscars.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，因为那时我才三岁，我根本不关心奥斯卡。

sentences.en: But I didn't want that to be a point against me.
sentences.zh: 但我不想让这成为扣分项。

sentences.en: So they had to like ask me, you know, different questions.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不得不问我一些不同的问题。

sentences.en: And I think that's the another hard part about testing age, Sam, is that you've got these age groups who can remember different things at different times.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是测试超忆症的另一个难点，因为不同年龄段的人能记住不同时期的不同事物。

sentences.en: So it's not only the interests, but it's the ages, because even if I can remember in 2005 and there's like a political event that took place, a fifth grader doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 所以不仅是兴趣问题，还有年龄问题，因为即使我能记住2005年发生的一件政治事件，一个五年级学生根本不在乎。

sentences.en: And probably if I was, you know, I was privileged enough to probably not even have to care at the time if it didn't affect my population.
sentences.zh: 而且如果我当时有幸不用关心这些，如果它没有影响到我的群体，我可能根本就不会去记。

sentences.en: And so that can be, I think, really difficult, too.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这确实也非常困难。

sentences.en: And that's what we ran into in the testing a lot was like there are just some events that they had asked that were in my time frame, but I didn't hear about, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们在测试中经常遇到这种情况，就是他们问到的一些事件确实在我记忆的时间范围内，但我却没听说过，你知道，

sentences.en: in sixth grade.
sentences.zh: 在六年级的时候。

sentences.en: But they were able to do some replacements.
sentences.zh: 但他们能够做一些替换。

sentences.en: It sounds a little bit like you were studying to go on Jeopardy.
sentences.zh: 听起来有点像你在为参加《危险边缘》节目做准备。

sentences.en: Yeah, a little bit, a little bit.
sentences.zh: 是啊，有一点，有一点。

sentences.en: But just like, again, getting my brain in that mode, because I knew I could do it.
sentences.zh: 但就像我说的，再次让我的大脑进入那种模式，因为我知道我能做到。

sentences.en: I wasn't like memorizing dates or anything.
sentences.zh: 我并不是在死记硬背日期什么的。

sentences.en: It was just kind of getting in that like recall mode where I could go kind of fast with it.
sentences.zh: 这只是进入了一种回忆模式，让我可以快速地进行回忆。

sentences.en: So there was that, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以就是那样，你知道。

sentences.en: Dr. Yasser, what do we know about the causes of HCM?
sentences.zh: Yasser 博士，我们对 HCM 的成因了解多少？

sentences.en: Is there a genetic component to it or any other hints about the etiology?
sentences.zh: 它有遗传因素吗，或者还有其他关于病因的线索吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we're trying to get to the bottom of the potential heritability.
sentences.zh: 我们正在努力探究其潜在的遗传性。

sentences.en: So we don't think it's a direct genetic component, as in if somebody has it, they're going to pass it on to their children.
sentences.zh: 我们认为它没有直接的遗传成分，也就是说，如果某人患有此症，并不意味着一定会传给他们的孩子。

sentences.en: But interestingly, in some of the cases, it turns out that there's also kind of, you know, extended family, relatives, cousins, maybe who have some traces of it as well.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，在某些病例中，你会发现，你知道，大家庭成员、亲戚、表亲中，可能也有人表现出一些迹象。

sentences.en: So it's a complex heritability pattern, if there is one.
sentences.zh: 所以如果存在遗传的话，那也是一种复杂的遗传模式。

sentences.en: And we're working with some colleagues who are really exceptional in terms of working on genetics to try to reveal the basis of this.
sentences.zh: 我们正在与一些在遗传学领域非常出色的同事合作，试图揭示其背后的基础。

sentences.en: Interestingly, one thing that might give us some clues is a set of identical twins.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，有一组同卵双胞胎可能为我们提供了一些线索。

sentences.en: And one of them has it, the other one does not.
sentences.zh: 其中一个患有此症，而另一个没有。

sentences.en: So it automatically tells us that it cannot be genetically inherited directly, because otherwise they would share that.
sentences.zh: 这自动告诉我们，它不可能是直接遗传的，否则他们应该会有相同的表现。

sentences.en: But there may be something that happens after the sort of the original splitting of that DNA that might be different.
sentences.zh: 但在 DNA 最初分裂之后，可能发生了一些不同的事情。

sentences.en: And we're trying to get to the bottom of that.
sentences.zh: 我们正在努力查明这一点。

sentences.en: But it is complicated because we don't have a huge sample to teSt.
sentences.zh: 但这很复杂，因为我们没有足够大的样本来进行测试。

sentences.en: And certainly, even within that smaller sample, the number of folks where there might be a trace of heritability is even smaller.
sentences.zh: 当然，即使在那个较小的样本中，可能存在遗传迹象的人数就更少了。

sentences.en: So it's not entirely clear how much of it is heritable and how much of it is environmental.
sentences.zh: 所以，到底有多少是遗传的，有多少是环境因素造成的，目前还不完全清楚。

sentences.en: With respect to the onset, it does vary from individual to individual.
sentences.zh: 关于发病时间，因人而异。

sentences.en: Usually, there's sort of a precipitating period or event.
sentences.zh: 通常会有一个诱发期或诱发事件。

sentences.en: Usually, it's during adolescence where that kind of comes fully to fruition.
sentences.zh: 通常是在青春期，这种症状会完全显现出来。

sentences.en: And it may be sort of the first person's first realization that this is what's going on.
sentences.zh: 这可能是当事人第一次意识到发生了什么。

sentences.en: Or it may be that memories start to get really, really strong after a particular event that could be a big change.
sentences.zh: 也可能是因为在某个重大变化事件之后，记忆开始变得非常非常强烈。

sentences.en: It's possible that it's traumatic.
sentences.zh: 这可能是创伤性的。

sentences.en: It's possible that it's just kind of a big event that happened in the person's life that is highly salient, consequential, maybe a move or something like that.
sentences.zh: 也可能只是生活中发生的一件大事，非常突出、影响深远，比如搬家之类的。

sentences.en: And then, typically, folks would report that from that point onwards, they've had these experiences kind of be sealed more into their memories.
sentences.zh: 然后，通常人们会报告说，从那时起，这些经历就更深刻地印在了他们的记忆中。

sentences.en: So, Marky, are you aware of any relatives you have who also have HCM?
sentences.zh: 那么，Marky，你知道你的亲戚里有谁也患有 HCM 吗？

sentences.en: No, but at Marquette, when I was working with Dr. Nielsen in their psychology department,
sentences.zh: 没有，但在马凯特大学时，我和心理学系的 Nielsen 博士一起工作，

sentences.en: she asked a lot of questions about my parents and actually brought my mom in to do some cognitive testing in an interview.
sentences.zh: 她问了很多关于我父母的问题，甚至还请我妈妈来做了一些认知测试和访谈。

sentences.en: And what we found is that my mom is really good with verbal recall.
sentences.zh: 我们发现我妈妈的语言回忆能力非常好。

sentences.en: And she has a very strong autobiographical memory.
sentences.zh: 而且她有非常强的自传体记忆。

sentences.en: Not as strong as mine, like remembering certain dates.
sentences.zh: 虽然不像我那样能记住具体的日期。

sentences.en: But if you ask her, she could tell you about events, where we sat when we were at this concert, or what was going on in our family last Christmas, or whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 但如果你问她，她能告诉你关于事件的细节，比如我们在那场音乐会上坐在哪里，或者去年圣诞节我们家里发生了什么，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Because my dad was already passed away by the time that we realized I had HSAM, and there was a name to call it.
sentences.zh: 因为在我意识到自己患有 HSAM 并给它命名时，我父亲已经去世了。

sentences.en: And so he died the same year I found out I had HSAM, so a couple months before.
sentences.zh: 他去世的那年正好是我发现自己患有 HSAM 的那一年，就在几个月前。

sentences.en: But what we remember about my father is he had an incredible ability to remember numbers.
sentences.zh: 但我们对父亲的记忆是他有惊人的数字记忆能力。

sentences.en: He knew people's addresses from his childhood, people's phone numbers from his childhood that he didn't need anymore.
sentences.zh: 他记得童年时期的地址、童年时期的电话号码，尽管他已经不再需要这些了。

sentences.en: He had our whole family's social security numbers memorized, you know, that he could just say.
sentences.zh: 他背下了我们全家人的社会安全号码，你知道，张口就来。

sentences.en: And so, you know, he had that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他有那种能力。

sentences.en: And then my mom had the memory thing.
sentences.zh: 而我妈妈有那种记忆力。

sentences.en: So it's kind of interesting how, for me, those kind of combine in like a memorization of numbers, or an ability to remember numbers, like dates.
sentences.zh: 所以很有趣，对我来说，这些能力结合在一起，就变成了对数字的记忆，或者说记住数字（如日期）的能力。

sentences.en: And then also the autobiographical part of it as well.
sentences.zh: 当然还有自传体记忆的部分。

sentences.en: I understand there are some links between HSAM and some mental health conditions.
sentences.zh: 我听说 HSAM 和一些心理健康状况之间存在联系。

sentences.en: Markie, you've written about the connection between your HSAM and obsessive-compulsive disorder.
sentences.zh: Markie，你写过关于你的 HSAM 和强迫症之间联系的文章。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的，可以。

sentences.en: So I really feel like my HSAM and OCD are pretty heavily linked.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得我的 HSAM 和强迫症联系非常紧密。

sentences.en: And it's because any time after I got diagnosed with OCD, people would be like, what are you obsessed with?
sentences.zh: 这是因为在我被诊断出强迫症后的任何时候，人们都会问，你对什么着迷？

sentences.en: What are you obsessed with?
sentences.zh: 你对什么着迷？

sentences.en: And I honestly didn't know.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道。

sentences.en: I was just like, I have compulsions, and I feel like I have to do things, and I have a lot of anxiety, and I have a tendency to hoard things, you know,
sentences.zh: 我只是说，我有强迫行为，我觉得我必须做某些事情，我有很大的焦虑，而且我有囤积东西的倾向，你知道，

sentences.en: all things I've been treated for and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我接受过治疗的问题等等。

sentences.en: But then as I started working with my, you know, with HSAM and stuff, I realized my obsession was dates, dates and calendars, and my own events in my life.
sentences.zh: 但后来当我开始处理我的 HSAM 等问题时，我意识到我的痴迷对象是日期、日历，以及我生活中发生的事件。

sentences.en: Because, you know, what it kind of helped me do, but it helped the OCD flourish in a lot of ways when I was younger, because I could remember exactly how something happened,
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，它在某种程度上帮助了我，但在我年轻的时候，它也在很多方面助长了强迫症，因为我能准确地记住事情是如何发生的，

sentences.en: and then I'd create a ritual to reinforce it.
sentences.zh: 然后我会创造一个仪式来强化它。

sentences.en: So what would happen was, let's say I wore a particular shirt the day I was taking a math test I was really nervous about.
sentences.zh: 所以会发生这样的事，假设我在参加一场让我非常紧张的数学考试那天穿了一件特定的衬衫。

sentences.en: Because of my memory, I could remember, you know, everything I did that day, the shirt I wore, what I ate for breakfast, you know, who I talked to that day.
sentences.zh: 因为我的记忆力，我能记住那天我做的一切，我穿的衬衫，我早餐吃了什么，我和谁说过话。

sentences.en: And then the part of my brain that had, you know, was responsible for my OCD would be like, all right, well, next time you've got a math test, if you want to get an A,
sentences.zh: 然后我大脑中负责强迫症的部分就会说，好吧，下次你再有数学考试，如果你想拿 A，

sentences.en: guess who you have to talk to?
sentences.zh: 猜猜你必须和谁说话？

sentences.en: Guess what you have to eat for breakfast?
sentences.zh: 猜猜你早餐必须吃什么？

sentences.en: Guess what you have to wear?
sentences.zh: 猜猜你必须穿什么？

sentences.en: And it started reinforcing that.
sentences.zh: 它就开始强化这一点。

sentences.en: So I think my memory played a large role into creating a lot of rituals that I was kind of slave to for a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我的记忆力在创造许多我长期以来一直受其奴役的仪式方面发挥了很大作用。

sentences.en: Dr. Yes, is that common among the people you work with?
sentences.zh: Yes 博士，这在你合作的人群中常见吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对常见。

sentences.en: So we see elements of this, perhaps maybe not at the level of a full diagnosis of obsessive-compulsive disorder, but certainly obsessive tendencies and obsessions,
sentences.zh: 我们看到了这些因素，也许还没达到完全诊断为强迫症的程度，但肯定有强迫倾向和强迫观念，

sentences.en: so the thoughts themselves.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些想法本身。

sentences.en: That seems to be much more highly represented in the group with HSAM.
sentences.zh: 这在患有超忆症（HSAM）的群体中似乎表现得更为显著。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's interesting, actually, for me, really, to hear Markey speak about it, because we've struggled to try to understand the causality chain.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对我来说，听到Markey谈论这件事真的很有趣，因为我们一直在努力理解其中的因果链。

sentences.en: In other words, is it that those two are sort of co-occurring conditions, and they're sort of feeding off of one another in some individuals, maybe to an extent, but not others?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这两者是否属于某种共存的状况，在某些个体中，它们是否在一定程度上相互促进，而在其他人身上则不然？

sentences.en: Or is one actually leading to the other?
sentences.zh: 还是说其中一个实际上导致了另一个？

sentences.en: In other words, if there's evidence of obsessions that are related to dates, if that happens in any individual who might otherwise be, you know, perfectly fine,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果一个人在其他方面表现得完全正常，却出现了与日期相关的强迫症迹象，

sentences.en: does it lead to this HSAM condition?
sentences.zh: 这是否会导致超忆症（HSAM）的产生？

sentences.en: And we don't know the answer to that.
sentences.zh: 我们目前还不知道答案。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's going to be that simple or straightforward, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不知道事情是否会那么简单直接。

sentences.en: I do think that there are some interesting shared traits and shared mechanisms, especially, as Markey was talking about, obsessing over dates.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为存在一些有趣的共同特征和共同机制，特别是像Markey所说的那样，对日期产生强迫性关注。

sentences.en: And they become much more important, much more consequential, because you see the value, that kind of feedforward cycle can precipitate the condition,
sentences.zh: 它们变得更加重要、影响更加深远，因为当你看到其价值时，那种前馈循环可能会诱发这种状况，

sentences.en: can perhaps lead to higher levels of anxiety and higher levels of OCD, but also can make the HSAM abilities much more reinforceable.
sentences.zh: 或许会导致更高水平的焦虑和强迫症（OCD），但也可能使超忆症的能力得到更强的巩固。

sentences.en: So if you're practicing this often and thinking about it often, you can imagine, just like anything else, you're going to get better at it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你经常练习并经常思考它，你可以想象，就像其他任何事情一样，你会变得越来越擅长。

sentences.en: One thing that Markey mentioned earlier, which I love because I've heard it now from a number of our volunteers, is the notion of going back a year.
sentences.zh: Markey之前提到的有一点我非常喜欢，因为我已经从我们的多位志愿者那里听到过，那就是“回溯一年”的概念。

sentences.en: So saying, you know, today is April 16th.
sentences.zh: 比如，今天是4月16日。

sentences.en: What happened on April 16th, 2020?
sentences.zh: 2020年的4月16日发生了什么？

sentences.en: What about 2019?
What about 2018?
And we will often hear that, and it seems like, you know, kind of a strange thing maybe, but it is an archival mechanism.
sentences.zh: 我们经常听到这种说法，这看起来可能有点奇怪，但它确实是一种存档机制。

sentences.en: It's a way to kind of build a record of the past day by day.
sentences.zh: 这是一种逐日建立过去记录的方式。

sentences.en: So we're still trying to figure out what those organizational schemes might look like.
sentences.zh: 所以我们仍在试图弄清楚这些组织方案可能是什么样的。

sentences.en: But I'm fascinated that this game of going back a year is actually something that was commonly shared across a number of volunteers that we've spoken to.
sentences.zh: 但我很着迷于这种“回溯一年”的游戏，它实际上是我们采访过的多位志愿者所共有的特征。

sentences.en: You were both quoted in a Wall Street Journal article last summer about how the COVID lockdowns were affecting people's memory.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，《华尔街日报》的一篇文章引用了你们两人的话，谈到了新冠疫情封锁如何影响人们的记忆。

sentences.en: And as you talked about this, going back a year, going back a year and going back a year, what has the lockdown done to the memories of people with HSAM?
sentences.zh: 正如你们所谈到的，这种不断回溯一年的行为，封锁对超忆症患者的记忆产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: So if you're directing this at me, I can tell you just in generalities.
sentences.zh: 如果你是在问我，我可以告诉你一些概括性的情况。

sentences.en: And what we have heard from some of our volunteers is that they don't feel that their track record, their memory of the past is as good as it was.
sentences.zh: 我们从一些志愿者那里听到的是，他们觉得自己的记录，即对过去的记忆，不如以前那么好了。

sentences.en: Because there's not enough events and not enough things happening, not enough salient dates with real occurrences to be able to gravitate to.
sentences.zh: 因为没有足够的事件，没有足够多的事情发生，也没有足够多具有实际意义的显著日期来让他们去关注。

sentences.en: But we've heard the same thing also from everybody else.
sentences.zh: 但我们也从其他人那里听到了同样的事情。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's just limited to HSAM.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这不仅仅局限于超忆症患者。

sentences.en: I think it really is kind of almost like a memory fog that we're all experiencing because it has been so monotonous and we've all been stuck at home and locked down.
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上更像是一种我们都在经历的“记忆迷雾”，因为生活太单调了，我们都被困在家里并处于封锁状态。

sentences.en: There hasn't been enough experiences with novelty in them that our memory systems kind of gravitate to and say, this is important.
sentences.zh: 没有足够的新鲜体验让我们的记忆系统去关注并说：这很重要。

sentences.en: I need to store that for later use.
sentences.zh: 我需要把它存起来以备后用。

sentences.en: But I'd love to hear from Marky what her feelings have been also.
sentences.zh: 但我很想听听Markey的感受。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I would, too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也想听听。

sentences.en: Is it disconcerting that you don't have these hooks to grab onto?
sentences.zh: 没有这些可以抓取的钩子，是否会让你感到不安？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's I've really found it's just a portion of lockdown.
sentences.zh: 我发现这只是封锁期间的一部分。

sentences.en: And maybe it's because I live in Alabama.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为我住在阿拉巴马州。

sentences.en: So it looks a little different here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的情况看起来有点不同。

sentences.en: But, you know, last March is really vivid.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，去年三月真的很生动。

sentences.en: Last March when, you know, I remember like, you know, everything shutting down and all of like how that was playing out.
sentences.zh: 去年三月，我记得一切是如何关闭的，以及事情是如何发展的。

sentences.en: And like my last the last day, like the day we found out that like the university, Auburn University was going to shut down like March 13th.
sentences.zh: 比如最后一天，我们得知奥本大学要关闭的那天，也就是3月13日。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That was that Friday.
sentences.zh: 那是那个周五。

sentences.en: And then that Sunday on the 15th, all staff got an email like, hey, we're going to start doing some remote work.
sentences.zh: 然后到了15号那个周日，所有员工都收到了一封邮件，说我们要开始远程办公了。

sentences.en: And we're like, whoa, whoa, whoa, what's happening?
sentences.zh: 我们当时想：哇，哇，哇，发生了什么？

sentences.en: And I remember, you know, on the 11th, that Wednesday, I was seeing the movie Emma about the Jane Austen novel.
sentences.zh: 我记得在11号那个周三，我正在看根据简·奥斯汀小说改编的电影《爱玛》。

sentences.en: And it was, you know, I didn't know it was the last time I'd be sitting in a movie theater for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 我当时并不知道那是我很长一段时间内最后一次坐在电影院里了。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden my phone just starts buzzing and buzzing.
sentences.zh: 突然间，我的手机开始不停地嗡嗡作响。

sentences.en: I was like, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 我当时想：发生了什么事？

sentences.en: And the NBA is getting canceled.
sentences.zh: NBA比赛被取消了。

sentences.en: March Madness is getting canceled.
sentences.zh: “疯狂三月”被取消了。

sentences.en: And it was like, what's what's happening?
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就是：到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: But, man, I have to tell you, April is blurry.
sentences.zh: 但是，伙计，我必须告诉你，四月是一片模糊。

sentences.en: April is is gone.
sentences.zh: 四月已经消失了。

sentences.en: Like it's I remember Easter because we did like a family Zoom Easter, my boyfriend and I and then my two friends that are back in Indiana.
sentences.zh: 我记得复活节，因为我和男朋友，还有我在印第安纳州的两个朋友，我们一起进行了家庭Zoom复活节聚会。

sentences.en: We did we played Ticket to Ride virtually together one weekend, and that'll be a year ago on this coming Sunday.
sentences.zh: 有一个周末我们一起在线玩了《车票之旅》，这个周末算起来正好是一年前的那个周日。

sentences.en: So I remember that.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得那个。

sentences.en: But there's like very few events because when you're working from home and you're not and you're not even leaving your apartment, you know,
sentences.zh: 但除此之外几乎没有什么事件，因为当你居家办公，甚至除了去杂货店之外连公寓都不出的时候，你知道，

sentences.en: for anything besides going to the grocery store, it's it was murky.
sentences.zh: 一切都是模糊不清的。

sentences.en: But when it came back was Memorial Day weekend.
sentences.zh: 但到了阵亡将士纪念日周末，记忆又回来了。

sentences.en: Yeah, Memorial Day weekend of last year with not only having a holiday and things like that, but then the killing of George Floyd happened.
sentences.zh: 是的，去年阵亡将士纪念日周末，不仅因为有假期，还因为发生了乔治·弗洛伊德被杀事件。

sentences.en: And so that is like, I think, a big event for me that kind of like started the H-SAM again of like, OK, we're back.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，那对我来说是一个重大事件，它重新启动了我的超忆症，让我觉得：好吧，我们回来了。

sentences.en: Like and events started happening.
sentences.zh: 事件开始发生了。

sentences.en: Dr. Yasser, what is the practical application of your work in this area?
sentences.zh: Yasser博士，您在这一领域的研究有什么实际应用吗？

sentences.en: I mentioned in the intro and looking at at Alzheimer's kind of the opposite where people lose their autobiographical memory.
sentences.zh: 我在开场白中提到了阿尔茨海默病，这在某种程度上是相反的，人们会失去自传体记忆。

sentences.en: Is this going to help with that?
sentences.zh: 这会有助于解决这个问题吗？

sentences.en: We hope so.
sentences.zh: 我们希望如此。

sentences.en: And in particular, some of our colleagues have also kind of identified what we think is is the opposite scheme, what they call SDAM or severely deficient autobiographical memory.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我们的一些同事也确定了我们认为是相反的模式，他们称之为SDAM，即严重缺陷自传体记忆。

sentences.en: So this is my colleague Brian Levine and his laboratory have identified individuals who have very, very fuzzy records of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我的同事Brian Levine和他的实验室已经确定了一些对过去记录非常模糊的个体。

sentences.en: Now, they still do OK on other memory tests and OK in other facets of life.
sentences.zh: 他们虽然在其他记忆测试中表现尚可，在生活的其他方面也还行。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're not Alzheimer's patients or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 他们也不是阿尔茨海默病患者之类的。

sentences.en: But their record of the past is not as rich as most of us would have.
sentences.zh: 但他们对过去的记录并不像我们大多数人那样丰富。

sentences.en: So so it seems like there is sort of a continuum or maybe a bell shaped curve with two extremes here.
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来似乎存在一个连续体，或者说是一个有两个极端的钟形曲线。

sentences.en: And understanding the extremes always informs us about the process and the mechanism.
sentences.zh: 了解这些极端情况总是能让我们深入了解其过程和机制。

sentences.en: When the condition was first identified, Dr. McGaw, I think, is quoted as saying this might have us rewrite the textbooks and really rethink the way we think about memory,
sentences.zh: 当这种状况首次被发现时，我想McGaw博士曾说过，这可能会让我们重写教科书，并真正重新思考我们对记忆的看法，

sentences.en: because we've always grown in the field to think that memory is adaptive because it doesn't store everything.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在这个领域一直认为记忆是适应性的，因为它不会存储所有东西。

sentences.en: It leaves a lot out and really focuses on things that can be used for generalizable knowledge.
sentences.zh: 它会遗漏很多东西，真正专注于那些可用于通用知识的事物。

sentences.en: And in fact, there are lots of examples about how damaging it would be if we tried to store everything because we would not be able to generalize.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有很多例子表明，如果我们试图存储所有东西，那将是多么具有破坏性，因为我们将无法进行概括。

sentences.en: However, seeing and the experience of those with age, Sam, suggests otherwise, suggests that maybe we missed something in that original assessment
sentences.zh: 然而，超忆症患者的经历表明情况并非如此，这表明我们可能在最初的评估中遗漏了一些东西，

sentences.en: and that it is possible to generalize flexibly and be able to apply knowledge and have an exceptional track record of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 即灵活地进行概括、应用知识并拥有卓越的过去记录是可能的。

sentences.en: So at a from a fundamental neuroscience perspective alone, it's really informative to try to understand that condition.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅从基础神经科学的角度来看，试图理解这种状况是非常有启发性的。

sentences.en: And of course, once you understand the machine and how it works, you can start to understand also how it breaks down.
sentences.zh: 当然，一旦你了解了这台机器及其工作原理，你也可以开始了解它是如何发生故障的。

sentences.en: So I do think there's going to be a lot of applicability to conditions where we have memory loss, not just Alzheimer's disease,
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为，这对于我们出现记忆丧失的状况会有很大的适用性，不仅仅是阿尔茨海默病，

sentences.en: but a variety of different neuropsychiatric illnesses as well.
sentences.zh: 还包括各种不同的神经精神疾病。

sentences.en: So, Marky, I'm guessing that as a result of your work with Dr. Yas's lab, that you were able to meet other people like yourself with age, Sam.
sentences.zh: Markey，我猜由于你与Yasser博士实验室的合作，你能够见到其他像你一样的超忆症患者。

sentences.en: What was that like to finally meet somebody who has a memory like yours?
sentences.zh: 终于见到一个记忆力和你一样的人，那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: I would say that the first meeting was very dramatic because 60 Minutes Australia made it very dramatic.
sentences.zh: 我会说第一次见面非常戏剧化，因为澳大利亚的《60分钟》节目把它做得非常戏剧化。

sentences.en: But Dr. Yas is like, yeah, I think I've seen this video.
sentences.zh: 但Yasser博士说：是的，我想我看过这个视频。

sentences.en: But anyway, what did they do?
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，他们做了什么？

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So I met Becky, who is a lovely, lovely woman from Australia, from, I believe, Queensland, Australia.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了Becky，她是一位来自澳大利亚昆士兰州的可爱女士，

sentences.en: That has age, Sam as well.
sentences.zh: 她也患有超忆症。

sentences.en: And 60 Minutes Australia wanted to do a segment on her as being, at the time at least, the only Australian, and maybe still the only Australian with age, Sam.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚的《60分钟》节目想为她做一个专题，因为当时她是唯一一位，也许现在仍然是唯一一位患有超忆症的澳大利亚人。

sentences.en: And her dream was to meet another person with age, Sam.
sentences.zh: 她的梦想是见到另一个患有超忆症的人。

sentences.en: So they looked at kind of the prospective folks and noticed I was the closest one to her age and also a girl.
sentences.zh: 所以他们查看了潜在的人选，发现我是最接近她年龄且也是女性的人。

sentences.en: And so, you know, they thought it'd be good for us to meet.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为我们见面会很好。

sentences.en: So 60 Minutes and all their team flew my mom and I out to Los Angeles and we got to meet Becky.
sentences.zh: 于是《60分钟》节目组带着我和我妈妈飞往洛杉矶，我们见到了Becky。

sentences.en: And they did this very dramatic, like, walk-in scene of, like, me standing in a courtyard and, like, her walking in.
sentences.zh: 他们安排了一个非常戏剧化的入场场景，比如我站在庭院里，她走进来。

sentences.en: Like, it was The Bachelor or something.
sentences.zh: 就像《单身汉》节目一样。

sentences.en: And then also the hilarious part, too, is, like, and anyone listening to this who has filmed a TV show before will know this.
sentences.zh: 而且搞笑的部分是，任何听过这个故事并拍过电视节目的人都会知道这一点。

sentences.en: But they had to do that take, like, ten times.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不把那个镜头拍了十次。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I met her for the first time once.
sentences.zh: 所以我第一次见到她其实只有一次。

sentences.en: But I had to act as, like, surprised and shocked and in awe as, like, I did the first time.
sentences.zh: 但我必须表现得像第一次见到她那样惊讶、震惊和敬畏。

sentences.en: And, you know, Becky and I aren't TV actresses here.
sentences.zh: 而且，Becky和我又不是电视女演员。

sentences.en: Like, we're not trying to get big or anything.
sentences.zh: 我们也不是想出名什么的。

sentences.en: So it was just kind of funny as they're like, all right, act surprised again.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们说“好，再表现得惊讶一点”时，真的很好笑。

sentences.en: And we're like, okay.
sentences.zh: 我们只能说：好吧。

sentences.en: So, you know, it was kind of funny.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实有点滑稽。

sentences.en: But Becky and I did get to develop a relationship and become friends.
sentences.zh: 但Becky和我确实建立起了联系并成为了朋友。

sentences.en: And that was the actual meaningful part.
sentences.zh: 那才是真正有意义的部分。

sentences.en: And that was the first time I had met anyone.
sentences.zh: 那是我第一次见到任何人。

sentences.en: The second time was when I was doing a segment for Scientific American.
sentences.zh: 第二次是在我为《科学美国人》做专题节目的时候。

sentences.en: And they filmed us in New York City when I was a graduate student back in 2017.
sentences.zh: 2017年我还是研究生时，他们在纽约市拍摄了我们。

sentences.en: And I got to meet Joey and Nicole, who are both East Coasters with H-Sam.
sentences.zh: 我见到了Joey和Nicole，他们都是东海岸的超忆症患者。

sentences.en: And so meeting them was really awesome, too.
sentences.zh: 所以见到他们也很棒。

sentences.en: They didn't do the dramatic meet scene.
sentences.zh: 他们没有安排那种戏剧性的见面场景。

sentences.en: They kind of just had us all, like, in a, you know, in kind of a panel kind of mode and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 他们只是让我们像参加小组讨论那样坐在一起。

sentences.en: But it's really cool to meet others with H-Sam because you can talk about, like, similar experiences that you have because of your H-Sam that other people may not experience.
sentences.zh: 但见到其他超忆症患者真的很酷，因为你可以谈论由于超忆症而产生的相似经历，而其他人可能不会有这些经历。

sentences.en: You can make jokes with them, too.
sentences.zh: 你也可以和他们开玩笑。

sentences.en: You know, date-related jokes that are super fun.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些关于日期的笑话非常有趣。

sentences.en: And just, again, just relate to, you know, we all have friends that we relate to for certain things, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，再次强调，我们都有可以谈得来的朋友，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, if me and a friend are really into the NFL, you know, we're going to connect over that.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我和一个朋友都非常喜欢NFL，我们就会因此产生共鸣。

sentences.en: But there's only a handful of people in the world that you can connect over this with.
sentences.zh: 但世界上只有少数人能和你在这方面产生共鸣。

sentences.en: And so it's really special when you get to meet.
sentences.zh: 所以能见面真的很特别。

sentences.en: Dr. Yasser, where is this research going next?
sentences.zh: Yasser博士，这项研究接下来会往什么方向发展？

sentences.en: What's the big question you would still like to answer?
sentences.zh: 您最想回答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: So there's a few avenues that we're pursuing.
sentences.zh: 我们正在追求几个方向。

sentences.en: One is that we would like to use more sort of validated tests to really fully assess the extent of H-Sam and be able to cater to different ranges of experiences and different ages,
sentences.zh: 一是我们希望使用更多经过验证的测试，来全面评估超忆症的程度，并能够适应不同范围的经历和不同年龄段，

sentences.en: as Marquis said.
sentences.zh: 正如Markey所说的那样。

sentences.en: So we've developed a couple of tools that we're able to use in children and adolescents that are not so time and era sensitive.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们开发了一些可以在儿童和青少年身上使用的工具，它们对时间和时代不那么敏感。

sentences.en: We've developed another one that is tapping into different areas of expertise.
sentences.zh: 我们还开发了另一种挖掘不同专业领域的工具。

sentences.en: And we're just in the process of validating those tests and making sure that they are reproducible and reliable and using them on a large enough data set so we can get a better feel for the prevalence of H-Sam.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于验证这些测试的过程中，确保它们具有可重复性和可靠性，并在足够大的数据集上使用它们，以便我们能更好地了解超忆症的患病率。

sentences.en: Second,
sentences.zh: 第二，

sentences.en: we would like to keep experimenting with neurobiology and really try to understand how is it that brains might be wired a little bit differently or have developed in a slightly different way to allow for these superior abilities to manifeSt.
sentences.zh: 我们希望继续进行神经生物学实验，真正试图理解大脑是如何以稍微不同的方式连接，或者以稍微不同的方式发育，从而使这些卓越的能力得以显现。

sentences.en: And that involves brain imaging studies, which we're embarking on.
sentences.zh: 这涉及我们正在着手进行的脑成像研究。

sentences.en: And then the third piece is the genetics and trying to really figure out if there is a heritable pattern and trying to figure out if there's something about gene environment interactions,
sentences.zh: 第三部分是遗传学，试图真正弄清楚是否存在遗传模式，并试图弄清楚基因与环境的相互作用是否存在某些因素，

sentences.en: perhaps in the earliest ages and during childhood and adolescence that allow for this to fully kind of come through.
sentences.zh: 也许是在最早的年龄段，以及在童年和青春期期间，使得这种能力能够完全显现出来。

sentences.en: So those are, I think, the three areas that we're mostly concerned with right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是我们目前最关心的三个领域。

sentences.en: And we're expanding to work with some collaborators who really do exceptional work in these areas to have a better handle on it.
sentences.zh: 我们正在扩大合作，与一些在这些领域做出杰出工作的合作者一起努力，以便更好地掌握它。

sentences.en: Last question to Marky.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题问Markey。

sentences.en: Are you glad you have this ability or would you give it up?
sentences.zh: 你很高兴拥有这种能力，还是愿意放弃它？

sentences.en: That's a hard question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难的问题。

sentences.en: It's really a hard one.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难回答。

sentences.en: And the answer lies somewhere in the middle.
sentences.zh: 答案介于两者之间。

sentences.en: And that's what I've had to come to in the choices I've had to make.
sentences.zh: 这就是我在必须做出的选择中不得不面对的结果。

sentences.en: Like, so when I found out that I had obsessive compulsive disorder, you know, I had the opportunity to start getting treatment, start getting medicated.
sentences.zh: 比如，当我发现自己患有强迫症时，我有机会开始接受治疗，开始服药。

sentences.en: And when I started getting medicated, my ability to recall as fast and quick and almost even sometimes accurately as I could started to go away.
sentences.zh: 当我开始服药时，我那种快速、即时，有时甚至非常准确的记忆能力开始减退。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I had to end up making the choice.
sentences.zh: 所以，我最终不得不做出选择。

sentences.en: Do I want to live with OCD and HSAM or do I want to not really live with a muted version of OCD and a muted version of HSAM?
sentences.zh: 我是想带着强迫症和超忆症生活，还是想过一种强迫症被抑制、超忆症也被削弱的生活？

sentences.en: And I chose living with the muted version because I'm a full functioning human being with dimensions to my wellness and to my life.
sentences.zh: 我选择了后者，因为我是一个功能健全的人，我的健康和生活都有着多维度的意义。

sentences.en: And I love having HSAM and the ability to go back in the past and recall and remember and cherish and savor those memories is so important to me.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢拥有超忆症，这种能够回到过去、回忆、铭记、珍藏并细细品味那些记忆的能力，对我来说非常重要。

sentences.en: But it can't get in the way of the rest of my life in my future.
sentences.zh: 但它不能阻碍我未来生活的其他部分。

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of like picking between the past and the future.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就像是在过去和未来之间做选择。

sentences.en: And it's a hard choice.
sentences.zh: 这是一个艰难的选择。

sentences.en: But, you know, I still have the ability.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我依然拥有这种能力。

sentences.en: Could it be, again, more entertaining on TV shows if I stopped my treatment for OCD?
sentences.zh: 如果我停止强迫症治疗，在电视节目上会不会更有看点？

sentences.en: Maybe, yeah.
sentences.zh: 也许会吧。

sentences.en: But is it worth it?
sentences.zh: 但值得吗？

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 不值得。

sentences.en: And so it's kind of hard, but I'm glad I'm at where I'm at now with balance.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实很难，但我很高兴我现在能达到一种平衡状态。

sentences.zh: 感谢两位今天来到这里。

sentences.zh: 很高兴能与你们交谈。
